title: 第1章 流浪法师林鬼第2章 信使系统
slug: 你好是寄往魔神堡垒的信吗
lines: 新约城，冒险者公会。
喧嚣声如热浪，裹挟着麦酒的酸涩与烟草的辛辣，在粗木梁柱间翻滚。
然而，当那道身影推开沉重的橡木门时，门口的声浪像骤然低伏下去。
他裹着一身洗得泛白、肘部磨损严重的深灰法袍。
宽大的兜帽压得很低，只露出几缕垂落的黑色碎发。
手中一柄看似朴素的橡木法杖，杖身却被岁月与掌心摩挲得温润。
他步履无声，穿过大厅。
所过之处，冒险者们举杯的动作凝滞，交谈化作压抑的窃语。
他径直走到柜台前，默不作声地，将一个沉甸甸的麻布口袋提上台面。
粗糙的布料上，浸染着深紫近黑的污渍，散发出淡淡的腥气。
袋口被扯开，一颗狰狞的头颅，暴露在昏黄的光线下。
暗红色的皮肤布满粗粝角质，空洞的眼窝似乎还残留着凶戾。
额前那对巨大、弯曲的镰刀状犄角，让空气瞬间凝固。
“是高阶巨镰角魔。”角落里一个沙哑声音艰难打破寂静。
“b级委托，95金币。”
“一个人……干掉需要整支白银团应付的恶魔……”
有人低声惊叹，语气中满是不可置信。
“流浪法师，无师自通，可惜，不懂人情世故。”
披着斗篷的老冒险者摇头评价。
“哼，连法师塔认证都没有，傲什么。”
穿着华丽铠甲的年轻战士不屑地撇嘴，声音却压得很低。
议论声刻意放大，交织酒气，带着明显的嫉妒与排挤。
然而没有人敢真正上前挑衅。
前台小姐怯生生推出钱袋，金币碰撞发出清脆声响。
“您的赏金，林鬼法师大人。”
她的手指微微发抖，低着头，不敢直视对方。
林鬼漠然接过，看都没看就塞入怀中，对身后嘈杂置若罔闻。
他转身走向贴满委托的公告板，袍角划出一道冷淡弧线。
魔法之路，每一寸精进，都需金币铺就，这是他十年来最深刻的体会。
板上任务光怪陆离。
剿灭鼠巢（1金）、寻猫（10金）、贵族家教（30金）、高墙教官（5金）、讨伐恶魔（15金起）、护送贵族至卡兰城（3000金）.....
……尽是富豪权贵悬赏，平民委托寥寥无几。
这个世界从来如此，金钱、权力、力量主宰一切。
他的目光漫不经心扫过角落，忽然定格在一张泛黄卷边的羊皮纸上。
它被钉在最不显眼的位置，边缘已经破损。
【信鸽】
类型：运输类
content_en:
New Testament City, Adventurers Guild.
The noise was like a heat wave, carrying the sourness of ale and the spiciness of tobacco, rolling between the thick wooden beams.
However, when the figure pushed open the heavy oak door, the sound at the door seemed to suddenly subside.
He was wrapped in a dark gray robe that had been washed white and the elbows were badly worn.
The wide hood was pulled down low, revealing only a few strands of hanging black hair.
There is a seemingly simple oak staff in his hand, but the body of the staff has been warmed by time and the care of his palm.
He walked silently through the hall.
Wherever they passed, the adventurers' toasting movements froze, and their conversations turned into suppressed whispers.
He walked straight to the counter and silently lifted a heavy linen bag onto the counter.
The rough fabric was stained with deep purple and almost black stains, exuding a faint fishy smell.
The mouth of the bag was torn open, and a ferocious head was exposed in the dim light.
The dark red skin is covered with rough cuticles, and the hollow eye sockets seem to still contain ferocity.
The pair of huge, curved, sickle-shaped horns on his forehead made the air freeze instantly.
"It's a high-level giant scythe-horned demon." A hoarse voice from the corner struggled to break the silence.
"B-level commission, 95 gold coins."
"One person...kills a demon that requires an entire Silver Regiment to deal with..."
Someone exclaimed in a low voice, their tone full of disbelief.
"The wandering mage is self-taught without a teacher. Unfortunately, he doesn't understand the ways of the world."
The old adventurer in a cloak shook his head and commented.
"Hmph, you don't even have the Mage Tower certification, so why are you so proud?"
The young warrior wearing gorgeous armor curled his lips in disdain, but kept his voice low.
The discussion was deliberately amplified, smelling of alcohol, with obvious jealousy and rejection.
However, no one dared to actually step forward to provoke.
The lady at the front desk timidly pushed out the money bag, and the gold coins collided with each other and made a crisp sound.
"Your bounty, Lord Lin Kuei Mage."
Her fingers were trembling slightly and she lowered her head, not daring to look directly at the other person.
Lin Gui took it indifferently, stuffed it into his arms without looking at it, and turned a deaf ear to the noise behind him.
He turned around and walked towards the bulletin board filled with commissions, the corner of his robe drawing a cold arc.
On the road to magic, every inch of progress is paved with gold coins. This is his most profound experience in ten years.
The tasks on the board are all kinds of weird.
Destroy rat nests (1 gold), search for cats (10 gold), noble tutors (30 gold), high-wall instructors (5 gold), defeat demons (from 15 gold), escort nobles to Kalan City (3,000 gold)...
...There are only bounties offered by the rich and powerful, and there are very few commissions from civilians.
This world has always been like this, money, power, and strength dominate everything.
His gaze casually swept around the corner, and suddenly settled on a piece of parchment with yellowed curls.
It was nailed in the most inconspicuous place and the edges were frayed.
【Homing Pigeon】
